pool.text: Portuguese explorers landed and named the area Ilha dos Patos.
The island was renamed to Ilha de Santa Catarina.
Official settlement began with the arrival of Francisco Dias Velho's company.
Construction of a chapel consecrated to Nossa Senhora do Desterro took place.
The Portuguese Crown elevated Santa Catarina Island to the category of village.
The settlement was promoted to the category of town.
The Capitania da Ilha de Santa Catarina was created with Desterro as capital.
Desterro became the Capital of Santa Catarina Province during the monarchy.
The state capital was renamed from Desterro to Florianópolis.
The Mercado Público de Florianópolis started operating as a public market.
The Hercílio Luz Bridge was built as a symbol of the island.
The Carijós Ecological Station was established by decree in the municipality.
The Marinha do Arvoredo Biological Reserve conservation unit was established.
Newsweek placed the location in its ten most dynamic cities list.
The Rio Vermelho State Park was created in the northeast of the island.
The New York Times reported the city as the party destination.
The gross domestic product for the city reached R$323,264,000,000.
The per capita income for the city reached R$45,602.
The city was ranked as the safest capital to live in Brazil.
